findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not compile
findings.body: The new condition calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only overload added in UsernamePasswordForm is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, and nothing in this diff adds a no-arg version. The services module will fail to compile, so the PR cannot be merged as is.

findings.title: Conditional passkey UI is now filled only when a user is already set, inverting the previous behavior
findings.body: Previously `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` ran when no user had been identified yet (`context.getUser() == null`), which is when the username/passkey conditional UI is needed on the first login page. The new guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` requires `user != null`, so on a fresh login the WebAuthn challenge and conditional-UI attributes are never set. The same inversion appears in the `challenge(context, error, field)` override (around line 137), which now fills only when a user is set. The intent was to fill when the user is present for re-authentication, but the no-user path that the existing tests (e.g. passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey expecting the webauth form on the initial page) rely on is broken.

findings.title: Negative element checks catch every Exception, so they can pass when they should not
findings.body: In reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey the `try { assertThat(findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee)` pattern catches any Exception, including unrelated WebDriver or matcher failures, so the check can silently pass for the wrong reason. Using `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` as the other tests in this PR do would make the assertion precise. The same pattern is repeated at lines 312-317 and in the other tests.
